units.text: “And it shall be after these things, that I will pour out of My Spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your elders shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.
Even upon male slaves and female slaves in those days I will pour out of My Spirit.
I will give wonders in heaven and upon the earth: blood, fire and a vapor of smoke.
The sun will turn to darkness and the moon to blood before the coming of the Lord’s great and manifest day.
Everyone who calls upon the Lord’s name will be saved, for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be one who escapes, as the Lord said, and bearers of good news whom the Lord has called.”

The number of Israel’s sons was like the sand of the sea, which will not be measured or counted. In the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ there they will be called sons of the living God.
Judah’s sons and Israel’s sons will gather together, appoint one authority for themselves and come up from the land, for great is Jezreel’s day.
Say to your brother, ‘My People,’ and to your sister, ‘Shown Mercy.’
I will remove the names of the Baalim from her mouth, and they will certainly no longer remember their names.
On that day I will establish a covenant for them with the field’s beasts, heaven’s birds and the earth’s creeping things. I will shatter bow, sword and war from the land and settle you in hope.
I will betroth you to Myself forever; I will betroth you to Myself in righteousness and judgment, in mercy and compassion,
and I will betroth you to Myself in faithfulness, and you will know the Lord.
On that day,” says the Lord, “I will listen to heaven, and heaven will listen to the earth,
and the earth will listen to grain, wine and oil, and they will listen to Jezreel.
I will sow her for Myself upon the land, show mercy to Not Shown Mercy and say to Not My People, ‘You are My people.’ He will say, ‘Thou art the Lord my God!’”
I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you will be cleansed from all your uncleannesses and all your idols. I will cleanse you.
And I will give you a new heart, and I will give a new spirit within you; and I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh, and give you a heart of flesh.
I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My ordinances, keep My judgments and do them.
“Therefore look, I am leading her astray; I will place her in a wilderness and speak to her heart,
and from there I will give her her possessions and the Valley of Achor to open her understanding. There she will be humbled as in the days of her infancy and the days of her ascent from Egypt’s land.
On that day,” says the Lord, “she will call Me ‘My Husband’ and no longer call Me ‘Baalim.’
I will remove the names of the Baalim from her mouth, and they will certainly no longer remember their names.

And if your brother, the son of your father or of your mother, or your son, or your daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or your friend who is as your own soul, entices you secretly, saying: Let us go and serve other gods, which you have not known, you nor your fathers,
of the gods of the nations round about you, whether near unto you or far from you, from one end of the earth unto the other,
you shall not consent unto him, neither shall you hearken unto him; neither shall your eye spare him, nor shall you yearn for him, nor conceal him.
You shall surely report him; your hands shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people.
And they shall stone him with stones, and he shall die; for he sought to turn you away from the Lord your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
And all Israel shall hear and fear, and shall no more do such an evil thing among you.
But the prophet who shall act ungodly, speaking in My name a word which I commanded him not to speak, or who shall speak in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.
And if you say in your heart: How shall we know the word which the Lord has not spoken?

Whatsoever the prophet speaks in the name of the Lord, if the word does not come to pass, nor is fulfilled, that is the word which the Lord has not spoken. That prophet has spoken in ungodliness; you shall not spare him.
He spoke to them, saying, ‘What was the character of the man who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?’
They said to him, ‘A hairy man, with a leather belt fastened around his waist.’ He said, ‘This is Elijah the Tishbite.’
Amos answered Amaziah, “I was no prophet or prophet’s son, but a goat herder and one who scratches sycamore figs,
and the Lord took me from the sheep, and the Lord said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’
After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus said to them, “All of you will stumble because of Me this night, for it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’
But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus said to them, “You will all stumble, because it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”
“And you, son of man, take a sword sharper than a barber’s razor. Obtain it for yourself and pass it over your head and your beard. Take a balance with weights and divide the hairs;

burn a quarter with fire inside the city when the days of siege are complete. Take a quarter and burn it up in its midst; cut down a quarter with the sword around it, and scatter a quarter to the wind. I will draw a sword after them.
Take a few of them in number and gather them into your cloak.
Take some of these again, cast them into the fire, and burn them in the fire. From it fire will go out. And you will say to the entire house of Israel,
For Thou didst test us, God; Thou didst try us by fire as silver is tried by fire.
Thou broughtest us into the trap; Thou didst place afflictions upon our back.
Thou madest human beings mount our heads; we passed through fire and water, and Thou broughtest us out to refreshment.

“Look, I am sending out My messenger, and he will look to a way before My face. Suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to His own sanctuary, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming,” says the Lord Almighty.
And who will endure the day of his entrance? Or who will stand at his appearance? For he enters like a smelting fire and like launderers’ herb.

He will sit, smelting and purifying as with silver and gold. He will cleanse the sons of Levi and melt them like gold and silver, and they will be those who bring a sacrifice to the Lord in righteousness.
And the sacrifice of Judah and Jerusalem will please the Lord, as in the days of old and as in the former years.
Then Moses and the sons of Israel sang this song to God, saying: “Let us sing to the Lord, for He has been gloriously glorified; horse and rider He has cast into the sea.
He has become a helper and a shelter to me for salvation; He is my God, and I will glorify Him; the God of my father, and I will exalt Him.
The Lord shatters wars; the Lord is His name.
Pharaoh’s chariots and his host He has cast into the sea; chosen riders, officers, He has drowned in the Red Sea.
With the sea He covered them; they sank into the deep as a stone.
Thy right hand, O Lord, has been glorified in strength; Thy right hand, O Lord, has shattered enemies.
The cherubim raised their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was upon them, above them.
The Lord’s glory rose from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain opposite the city.
A spirit lifted me and brought me into the Chaldeans’ land, to the captives, in a vision by God’s spirit. I rose out of the vision I had seen,
and I spoke to the captives all the Lord’s words that He had shown me.
After saying these things, He was lifted up as they watched, and a cloud took Him from their sight.
As they were gazing into heaven while He went, look—two men stood beside them in white garments.
They said, “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw Him go into heaven.”
Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mountain called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath’s journey away.
The words of Amos that came among nakkarim from Tekoa, which he saw concerning Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
Now may our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus, direct our way to you.
And may the Lord make you increase and overflow in love for one another and for all, just as we also do for you,
so as to establish your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His saints. Amen.
Injustice will no longer be heard in your land, nor destruction and misery within your borders. Your walls will be called Salvation, and your gates Engraving.
The sun will not be your light by day, nor will the rising moon light your night. Instead, the Lord will be your everlasting light and God your glory.
For your sun will not set, and your moon will not fail. The Lord will be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning will be fulfilled.
Your people will all be righteous, and they will inherit the land for ever, guarding the planting, the works of His hands, for glory.
The fewest will become thousands, and the least a great nation. I, the Lord, will gather them at the proper time.

He brought me to the house’s vestibules, and look—water was flowing out beneath the open court toward the east, for the house’s front faced east. The water was descending from the right side, from the south toward the altar.
He brought me out by the north gate and led me around outside to the court’s gate facing east. Look—the water was flowing down from the right side.
As the man went out opposite, with a measure in his hand, he measured a thousand with the measure and went through the water—water of release.
He measured a thousand and went through water up to the thighs. He measured a thousand and went through water up to the waist.
He measured a thousand and could not go through, for the water surged violently like the rush of a torrent that they will not cross.
He said to me, “Have you seen, son of man?” Then he led me to the river’s edge.
As I returned, look—very many trees were on the river’s edge, on both sides.
He said to me, “This water flowing out into eastern Galilee was descending into Arabia and coming as far as the sea, to the water of the outlet; it will heal the waters.

Every life among the swarming living creatures will live wherever the river comes. There will be very many fish there, because this water has arrived there, and it will become healthy and live. Everything over which the river comes will live.
Fishers will stand there from Aingadin to Ainagalim; there will be a drying place for nets. It will be by itself, and its fish will be like the fish of the Great Sea, an exceedingly great multitude.
At its outlet, at its turning, and at its overflow, they will certainly not be healed; they are given over to salt.

Along the river, on its edge on both sides, every edible tree will grow. Nothing upon it will grow old, nor will its fruit fail. In its newness it will bear its first crop, because these waters flow from the holy places. Their fruit will be for food and their growth for health.

And these are the ordinances and judgments which the Lord commanded the sons of Israel in the wilderness, when they came forth out of the land of Egypt: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.

There was terror in the camp and in the field. All the people in the messab and the destroyers were terrified, and they were unwilling to act. The earth was astonished, and there was terror from the Lord.
Saul’s lookouts in Benjamin’s Geba saw the camp in turmoil this way and that.
Saul said to the people with him, “Please muster and see who has gone from you.” They mustered, and Jonathan and the one carrying his equipment could not be found.
Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring the ephoud near.” For he was bearing the ephoud before Israel that day.
While Saul spoke to the priest, the sound in the foreigners’ camp kept growing louder. Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hands.”
Saul and all the people with him cried out and came to the battle. Each man’s sword was against his neighbour, with exceedingly great confusion.
When His praise of thanksgiving began, the Lord set the sons of Ammon to fight against Moab and Mount Seir, who had come out against Judah, and they were routed.
The sons of Ammon and Moab rose against Mount Seir’s inhabitants to destroy and wipe them out. When they had finished Seir’s inhabitants, they rose against one another to be destroyed.
Judah reached the wilderness lookout and looked out and saw the multitude. There they were: all dead, fallen on the ground, with no survivor.

Jehoshaphat and his people came to plunder their spoils. They found many herds, baggage, spoils, and precious articles, and plundered them for themselves. They spent three days plundering the spoils, because they were so many.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Feast of Tents unto the Lord for seven days.
And on the first day there shall be a holy convocation. You shall do no laborious work.

For seven days you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. The eighth day shall be a holy convocation for you, and you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. It is a closing observance; you shall do no laborious work.
You shall keep the Feast of Tents seven days, when you have gathered in from your threshing floor and from your winepress.

And you shall rejoice in your feast, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your male slave, and your female slave, and the Levite, and the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow within your cities.

You shall keep a feast for seven days unto the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for Himself; and if the Lord your God blesses you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, you shall rejoice.

Three times in the year shall every male among you appear before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord shall choose: in the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and in the Feast of Weeks, and in the Feast of the Pitching of Tents. You shall not appear before the Lord your God empty,
You shall make a plate of pure gold and stamp on it like a seal: ‘The Lord’s consecrated thing.’
You shall fasten it to spun blue material so that it may rest on the headband, at the front of the headband.

It shall be on Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron shall remove the sins of the holy things the sons of Israel consecrate, of every holy gift. It shall be on Aaron’s forehead continually, acceptable for them before the Lord.
Awake, awake, Zion! Clothe yourself with your strength, Zion, and put on your glory, Jerusalem, holy city. No uncircumcised and unclean person will pass through you again.
